1  QUASH the same and all other proceedings and pass such other or oth  orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and necessary in the  circumstances of the case.
For Petitioners : M/s.Ashok Kumar  For Respondents : Mr.A.Damodaran,Addl.

Public Prosecut  : M/s.K.R.Ramesh Kumar [R.2]
 ORDER

The petition is to quash the FIR for the alleged offences under Sections 406, 420 & 34 of IPC.
2.

It is alleged in the FIR that the petitioner who was the then Chairman/Director of the 1st accused company along with the other accused had mortgaged a property in which the de facto complainant had a share; that the accused had mortgaged the property without the consent of the de facto complainant.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the property was mortgaged with the consent of the de facto complainant and this is fortified by the fact that subsequently the mortgaged property was sold and the sale proceeds were shared by both the de facto complainant and the accused company and therefore, nothing survives for investigation in the instant FIR.
4.
The learned counsel for the de facto complainant submitted that it is true that pursuant to the sale of the property the de facto complainant received half of the sale consideration.
However, the complaint of the de facto complainant cannot be said to be false since the original mortgage was made without his knowledge.

5. This Court without going into the merits of the contentions of the learned counsels on either side is of the view that since the matter has been admittedly sorted out between the parties by sharing the sale proceeds of the disputed property, the 2nd respondent may not have any grievance in the instant issue.
Since there is no wrongful gain or wrongful loss to anybody the offences alleged would not be made out.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6.
In such view of the matter, no useful purpose would be served in keeping the impugned FIR pending investigation.
Hence, this Court in the interest of justice is inclined to quash the impugned FIR.
Hence, the impugned FIR is quashed.
7. Accordingly, the Criminal Original Petition is allowed.
Consequently, connected Criminal Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
